title: Implementing a Boolean Function on a Multiplexer
quickIdea: Put n-1 variables on the select lines and the leftover variable on the data inputs: each data input becomes 0, 1, the variable, or its complement, read off a two-row table.
remember: An n-variable function needs a 2^(n-1)-to-1 multiplexer plus one inverter, because each data input is a function of the one remaining variable and only four cases arise: 0, 1, X, X'.
Reading rule for the pair of rows that share a select code, where the leftover variable X = 0 is the upper row: both 0 gives I = 0; both 1 gives I = 1; 0 then 1 gives I = X; 1 then 0 gives I = X'.
With a full 2^n-to-1 multiplexer and all n variables on the select lines no extra hardware is needed at all: tie I_k to the function's value at minterm k.

Sizing consequence: 2^(n-1)-to-1 plus one inverter always suffices (GATE CSE 2007 Q.34); 2^(n-2)-to-1 does not, because each data input would then be a function of two leftover variables and one inverter cannot produce all sixteen of them.
Order matters: the variable on S_{n-2} is the more significant of the select bits, so the minterm indices run in that variable's order - get it backwards and every data input is wrong.
The same method works in reverse: given the data inputs, expand the multiplexer equation and minimise to read the function (GATE CSE 2014 Set 1 Q.45).

example.prompt: GATE CSE 2021 Set 2 Q.5. Implement f(x,y,z) = m0 + m1 + m3 + m4 + m5 + m6 on a 4-to-1 multiplexer whose select lines are y and z, leaving x as the data variable.
example.work: Index by x y z, so the select code yz fixes the pair of minterms that differ in x. yz = 00 gives m0 and m4, both of which are 1, so I0 = 1. yz = 01 gives m1 and m5, both 1, so I1 = 1. yz = 10 gives m2 = 0 and m6 = 1, so I2 = x. yz = 11 gives m3 = 1 and m7 = 0, so I3 = x'.
example.answer: I0 = I1 = 1, I2 = x, I3 = x' - the circuit of option (A).

gateAngle: This is the most-repeated multiplexer pattern in the papers: 2007 Q.34 asks for the smallest multiplexer that still works with one inverter, 2021 Set 2 Q.5 gives the function and asks for the data inputs, and 2014 Set 1 Q.45 gives the data inputs and asks for the minimal sum of products. All three are the same two-row table read in different directions.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Implement f(A,B,C) = m1 + m2 + m4 + m7 on a 4-to-1 multiplexer with A and B on the select lines.
variations.answer: I0 = C, I1 = C', I2 = C', I3 = C, and the function is A XOR B XOR C.
variations.why: A = 0, B = 0 gives m0 = 0 and m1 = 1, so the input is C. A = 0, B = 1 gives m2 = 1 and m3 = 0, so C'. A = 1, B = 0 gives m4 = 1 and m5 = 0, so C'. A = 1, B = 1 gives m6 = 0 and m7 = 1, so C. Two of the four inputs are complements of C, which is why one inverter suffices.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why is a 2^(n-1)-to-1 multiplexer with one inverter enough for any n-variable function, while 2^(n-2)-to-1 is not?
variations.answer: With n-1 select lines each data input is a function of one variable, and a single variable has only four possible functions - 0, 1, X, X' - all reachable with one inverter. With n-2 select lines each data input is a function of two variables, and there are sixteen of those, so real gates are needed.
variations.why: The count of functions of k variables is 2^(2^k): four for k = 1 and sixteen for k = 2. One inverter covers the four; it cannot cover the sixteen.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: The same function f(x,y,z) = m0 + m1 + m3 + m4 + m5 + m6 is implemented on a full 8-to-1 multiplexer with x, y, z on the select lines. What are the eight data inputs?
variations.why: Each data input is simply the value of the function at that minterm, with no leftover variable to fold in. This is the sanity check for the 4-to-1 answer: folding the pairs 0/4, 1/5, 2/6, 3/7 of 1,1,0,1,1,1,1,0 gives 1, 1, X, X' as required.

trap.what: Reading the pair of rows in the wrong order, which swaps X and X' on every data input.
trap.why: The leftover variable must be the most significant index bit for the rule 'upper row is X = 0' to hold. If x is treated as the least significant bit instead, the pairs become (0,1), (2,3), (4,5), (6,7) and the answers change.
trap.counterexample: For f = m0 + m1 + m3 + m4 + m5 + m6 read with yz as the low bits, the pairs are (0,1), (2,3), (4,5), (6,7) giving 1, X', 1, X - a different and wrong set of data inputs for this question, whose accepted answer is I0 = I1 = 1, I2 = x, I3 = x'.

check.question: For f = m1 + m3 + m5 + m7 of three variables, with y and z on the select lines and x left over, what are the four data inputs?
check.answer: I0 = 0, I1 = 1, I2 = 0, I3 = 1 - that is, I = z, because the function is simply z.
check.explanation: yz = 00 gives m0 = 0 and m4 = 0, so 0. yz = 01 gives m1 = 1 and m5 = 1, so 1. yz = 10 gives m2 = 0 and m6 = 0, so 0. yz = 11 gives m3 = 1 and m7 = 1, so 1. The odd minterms of three variables are exactly those with z = 1.

sourceLine: The Shannon-expansion reading and the construction of a bigger multiplexer from smaller ones: NPTEL IIT Kharagpur Lecture 16 (English). The data-input reading rule and the sizing rule are recomputed here and checked in scripts/validate.py against the three PYQs on this card: GATE CSE 2007 Q.34 (option C), 2014 Set 1 Q.45 (option A) and 2021 Set 2 Q.5 (option A).
